prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / editorial print design. Create ONE high-resolution image showing a beautifully art-directed yet technically feasible School Moves lesson PDF as TWO upright A4 portrait pages side by side, fully visible, straight-on flat front view on a pale lavender backdrop, subtle shadow and generous gutter. No devices, no tilted perspective. This is a proposed visual design only. School Moves identity: plum purple #482C53, soft lavender #DED5EB, citron #D5E75A, cloud #F6F5FA, charcoal #302A38. Sophisticated educational editorial design, crisp rounded sans serif, strong bold headings, generous margins, disciplined grid, fine rules, restrained curved movement motif. White paper dominates to preserve readable practical print. This must feel substantially more designed than a plain reportlab document yet use components possible with HTML-to-PDF: typography, rounded colour panels, tables, SVG field diagram, flat vector accents. NO photographs, no complex effects, no handwritten text, no arbitrary decorative clipart, no orange, no Zactiv. Shared School Moves symbol three rising rounded movement strokes. Text perfectly legible, use concise exact copy below without inventing extra lesson instructions.
LEFT PAGE is polished lesson overview. Compact header logo 'School Moves' with small line 'Confident teaching. Active schools.' Small running metadata 'YEAR 3 / FOOTBALL / WEEK 1'. Large title 'Introduction to football' on white, bold plum, a restrained citron movement accent tucked into upper right margin. Subtitle 'Shielding, ball control and beating a player'. Elegant horizontal metadata strip '30 children' / 'Outdoor' / '45+ cones / 30 balls'. A two-column panel: 'Learning objectives' bullet 'Shielding the ball' 'Ball manipulation' 'Beat-the-player moves'; second 'Whole child' bullet 'I can persevere' 'I can follow the rules' 'I can take turns'. Lower half 'Your lesson at a glance' with three attractive structured rows, numbered plum circles, duration pills and clear activity names: '01 Escape the Castle' 'Warm-up · 15 min'; '02 Captain Hook' 'Challenge 1 · 20 min'; '03 Beat the player tunnel' 'Challenge 2 · 10–15 min'. Citron-accented narrow teacher reminder box 'Remember the horseshoe technique.' Tiny timing note 'Activity blocks: 45–50 min. Reflection and transitions are untimed.' Footer thin plum rule and 'School Moves · Design concept' left / '01' right. Plenty of breathing room, no cover-only wasted page.
RIGHT PAGE is activity delivery sheet. Same brand running header. Small eyebrow 'WARM-UP / 15 MIN'. Large plum title 'Escape the Castle'. Compact lavender setup strip '30 × 30 area · Groups of four · 1 ball and 6 cones per group'. Main upper row: left column 'How to run it' with three numbered short paragraphs 'Make three gates with six cones. Three players guard the gates; one starts in the middle.' 'On “3, 2, 1, go”, the middle player tries to escape without being tagged.' 'Gate players move side to side. Swap roles after an escape.' Right column a large clean SVG-style overhead diagram on a very pale lavender rectangular field: six citron triangle cones forming three gates around a central pale purple player, one dark plum gate player at each gate, one dashed arrow from middle through a gate. Under diagram simple legend 'Player / Middle player / Cone'; no green football field. Lower section two clearly designed boxes: lavender 'Teaching cues' with 'Use the inside, outside and sole of the foot.' 'Keep the ball under control.' 'Ask how the group took turns.'; white outlined 'Progression' with 'Add a ball: dribble out under control.' 'Gate players tag; they do not tackle.' 'Adjust gate width to change the challenge.' Bottom short fine-print 'Condensed layout example. Confirm full instructions and diagram before use.' Footer thin rule, 'School Moves · Design concept' / '02'. Hierarchy consistent across both pages, no overflowing text, all body text readable, attractive citron label accents, page numbers. Deliver image only, not a PDF file.
